idiom_name: Jakarta REST resource method returning Response
implementation_notes: In Jakarta REST (or a plain HttpServlet) the Action is a resource method annotated @GET/@Path whose parameters are bound from the request, and the Responder role is the returned jakarta.ws.rs.core.Response builder (status, headers, entity) or the HttpServletResponse the container writes. The Domain must be an injected service that never receives HttpServletRequest. Keep the class-per-action split when one endpoint answers in several media types: one responder component per format then replaces the inline Response builder, which otherwise mixes format choice into the action.
pitfalls: JAX-RS resource classes are per-request instances but Spring beans are singletons: mutable fields on a singleton handler are a concurrency bug.
Returning the domain entity directly leaks lazy-loading and persistence semantics into the response; map to a DTO in the responder.

Using @Produces as if it controlled every manually built Response -> an entity without a matching writer or explicit media type can yield 406 or an unexpected representation -> map to a DTO and set the response media type explicitly when bypassing provider selection.

variants.name: Spring WebFlux functional endpoint (HandlerFunction + ServerResponse)
variants.implementation_notes: Spring WebFlux.fn makes the split explicit in the type signatures: a HandlerFunction<ServerResponse> is the Action (ServerRequest in, Mono<ServerResponse> out), ServerResponse.ok()/notFound() builders are the Responder, and RouterFunctions.route(GET("/users/{id}"), handler) is the one-handler-per-route dispatch. Choose it when you want the roles visible without annotations and reflection, and a Java 17+ baseline; choose annotated controllers when the team expects Spring MVC conventions.
pitfalls: Blocking calls (JDBC, file I/O) inside a HandlerFunction block the event loop; wrap them or stay on the MVC stack.
ServerResponse is immutable - dropping the builder's return value silently produces no response.
Errors must be signalled through the reactive chain (onErrorResume, error attributes); thrown exceptions bypass the response builder.
